deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. Despite the bundle label, it is not a Riemann manuscript. It is the second page (folio 30v) of a letter from Karl Hattendorff, dated Aachen, 9 November 1875 (the date is on the previous page). The recipient is very probably Heinrich Weber, then editing Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876). The page continues the previous one, where Hattendorff sends a short introduction to Riemann's paper on minimal surfaces for the collected edition. He proposes it could end at 'in dieselbe Zeit fallen'. Alternatively a longer ending could be used that mentions H. A. Schwarz, beginning 'Die von Weierstrass auf der einen, etc.'.

On this page Hattendorff says that if Schwarz is mentioned, he wants his friend Schondorff mentioned too. Schondorff's prize essay stands to Riemann as Schwarz's prize essay stands to Weierstrass. This refers to the Göttingen faculty prize work on the minimal surface bounded by a skew quadrilateral, published 1868, which worked out Riemann's method. Hattendorff encloses a copy of Schondorff's treatise and says it will surely not displease Weber.

He then asks, ironically, that Weber 'enjoy' the flowery style of the 'great heir of Gauss's residence' in the judgment of the Philosophical Faculty. This is the faculty's prize report; the jibe is probably aimed at Ernst Schering, who lived in Gauss's quarters at the Göttingen observatory. That identification is my inference.

He leaves it to Weber whether to print the short or the somewhat longer introduction. Finally he encloses a Riemann manuscript on the potential of a ring, which he received from Dedekind. He judged it better suited to the Gesammelte Werke than to his own edition of Riemann's potential-theory lectures (Schwere, Elektricität und Magnetismus, 1876). He closes with greetings, signed K. Hattendorff.

The page matters for the editorial history of Riemann's Werke: the introduction to the minimal-surface paper, the crediting of Schwarz and Schondorff, and the provenance of the fragment on the potential of a ring (Dedekind → Hattendorff → Weber). There are no derivations to reconstruct.

results.what: Editorial correspondence: proposal to credit Schondorff alongside Schwarz in the introduction to Riemann's minimal-surface paper in the Gesammelte Werke
results.modern_name: History of the Riemann–Weierstrass–Schwarz treatment of the Plateau problem for a skew quadrilateral (Schwarz–Riemann minimal surface)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (posthumous paper, edited by Hattendorff, 1867); Schwarz (1865/1871); Schondorff (Göttingen prize essay, 1868)

results.what: Provenance of Riemann's manuscript on the potential of a ring (from Dedekind via Hattendorff to the editor of the Werke)
results.modern_name: Riemann, 'Über das Potential eines Ringes' (Nachlass piece in Gesammelte Werke)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a letter from Hattendorff to the Werke editor about editorial matters, with no mathematical content. The facts it records (the Schwarz/Schondorff priority context, the ring-potential fragment) are known from the Werke and the history of their editing.
transcription_corrections: 'nicht ganz[?] einsehen[?] zu wollen' should read 'recht ge-/nießen zu wollen' (i.e. 'recht genießen zu wollen').
'über das Potential einer[?] Kugel[?]' should read 'über das Potential eines Ringes'; this matches the Werke piece 'Über das Potential eines Ringes'.
'großen Erben[?]' appears correct as 'großen Erben' ('der Gauß'schen Wohnung' follows on the next line).
The writer is K. Hattendorff, writing from Aachen in 1875, so the folio is a letter, not a Riemann autograph.
